fields.id: Stable slug, referenced by every record. Required.
fields.name: Human name of the source. Required.
fields.url: Landing page or file URL. Required.
fields.local_path: Path in this repo holding the snapshot, if any.
fields.adapter: Name of the adapter function that ingests it. Required.
fields.attribution: The citation string to reproduce when using it.
fields.retrieved: ISO date this snapshot was taken.
fields.scope: One line on coverage: geography, topic, period.
fields.record_kinds: Record kinds it can produce, from ('site_profile', 'site_capacity', 'site_compute', 'chip_spec', 'chip_price', 'chip_inventory', 'region_availability', 'benchmark_result', 'training_run', 'supply_metric', 'cost_model', 'reliability', 'geo_profile', 'citation'). Required.
fields.entity_types: Entity types it can create or describe, from ('company', 'accelerator', 'datacenter', 'cloud_region', 'component', 'country').
fields.fills: Dotted paths this source can populate, e.g. 'datacenter.power_mw'. Drives the fill step's precedence and the UI's 'fills' column. Required.
fields.trust: 0-1. Tie-breaker when two sources claim the same field. Primary/vendor/filing high, analyst model mid, aggregator low. Required.
fields.confidence_default: Confidence stamped on records lacking their own: ('confirmed', 'estimate', 'rumor').
fields.caveats: What this source is known to get wrong or omit.
fields.sample: Ids of representative records, filled by the builder.
fields.stats: {records, documents, entities, record_kinds{}} filled by the builder.

kinds.pipeline: An ingestion system with its own provenance model, ingested as a whole.
kinds.dataset: A published, downloadable dataset with a licence.
kinds.document-set: A set of individual documents (news, filings, vendor pages) cited per claim.
kinds.api: A queryable endpoint read at build time or snapshotted.
kinds.derived: A table produced by this repository from other sources.
kinds.registry: A directory or listing service used to enumerate facilities.

sources.name: dataCenterView pipeline export
sources.licence: As provided in the uploaded project
sources.scope: United States data centers with field-level provenance from an agentic discover → extract → cross-vendor verify pipeline.
sources.caveats: US-only, and 398 of 490 records are flagged needs_review upstream. capacity_mw is nameplate capacity, not energised load. Carries no accelerator counts: its compute layer is an illustrative seed.

sources.name: Epoch AI — AI Data Centers
sources.attribution: Epoch AI, 'AI Data Centers'. Published online at epoch.ai.
sources.scope: 83 frontier AI data centers worldwide with modelled power, H100-equivalents, capital cost, owners and users.
sources.caveats: Power, chip counts and capex are model outputs inferred from satellite imagery, permits and utility filings — not company disclosures. Coverage prioritises the US; no coordinates are published, so addresses must be geocoded.

sources.name: Epoch AI — data center build timelines
sources.scope: 492 dated observations of construction status, IT power and H100-equivalents per site, including future-dated build plans.
sources.caveats: The 'Construction status' column is a free-text observation note, not an enum — status must be derived from the numbers. Rows dated after the build date are projections.

sources.name: Epoch AI — per-site chip quantities
sources.attribution: Epoch AI, 'AI Data Centers' (chip quantities table).
sources.scope: 225 rows of chip type and unit count per site per date — the only public per-site accelerator census that exists.
sources.caveats: Counts are modelled from power and cooling capacity. Thirteen site names appear here but not in the main table; one duplicates another site under a different owner and is dropped by alias rule.

sources.name: Curated global sites
sources.licence: Repository licence; underlying claims belong to their publishers
sources.attribution: Assembled from company announcements, government publications and trade press; every row carries its own source URLs.
sources.scope: 95 sites in 31 countries that Epoch does not cover — EuroHPC, Nscale, Nebius, Humain, Stargate UAE, SoftBank, NAVER, Yotta, Huawei, Firmus, Bell, Scala, Cassava and others.
sources.caveats: Hand-assembled, so coverage reflects what was searched for. Each row states its own confidence: 61 confirmed, 27 estimate, 7 rumor.

sources.name: Cloud provider documentation and pricing APIs
sources.publisher: Google Cloud, AWS, Microsoft Azure, Oracle, CoreWeave
sources.attribution: Provider region/zone documentation and retail pricing APIs.
sources.scope: 53 cloud regions with the accelerator generations each can provision, and the physical metro serving each region.
sources.caveats: A region is a metro, not a building. Providers publish where a SKU can be provisioned, never how many chips are installed.

sources.name: Accelerator specification table
sources.attribution: Compiled from vendor datasheets and architecture whitepapers; see report/report.md for per-figure sourcing.
sources.scope: 49 accelerators from 12 vendors: process, memory, dense throughput at each precision, TDP, fabric, scale-up domain and unit price.
sources.caveats: All throughput figures are dense: vendor headline numbers that assume 2:1 sparsity have been halved. Unpublished values are blank rather than interpolated.

sources.name: Cloud accelerator pricing
sources.attribution: Vendor rate cards plus price trackers, per row.
sources.scope: 59 offers across 12 providers and 9 pricing tiers, per chip-hour.
sources.caveats: Marketplace and spot rows are host-set and volatile; the same silicon spans a 45x price range across tiers.

sources.name: Supply-chain metrics
sources.attribution: TrendForce, supplier disclosures, analyst estimates, per row.
sources.scope: CoWoS capacity and demand, HBM share and pricing, wafer prices, unit-shipment estimates and rack power, 2023-2027.
sources.caveats: No supplier reports HBM revenue separately, so share figures are estimates that disagree between sources by up to 20 points.

sources.name: Modelled bills of materials
sources.attribution: Raymond James teardown lineage, extended by Epoch AI, TrendForce and SemiAnalysis.
sources.scope: Six accelerators broken into logic die, HBM, packaging and assembly cost, with a modelled sell price.
sources.caveats: No vendor discloses per-part cost of goods; every figure is a model.

sources.name: MLPerf Training results
sources.licence: MLCommons results are public; table compiled here
sources.attribution: MLCommons MLPerf Training v4.0 through v6.0 result sets.
sources.scope: 29 audited time-to-train results by benchmark, platform and scale.
sources.caveats: Submitters choose their own scale, and the closed division has no perf-per-dollar or perf-per-watt metric.

sources.name: Rack and pod systems
sources.scope: 13 rack- and pod-scale systems: chips, compute, memory, fabric, power and price.
sources.caveats: A TPU superpod is ~128 racks' worth of chips, so per-system totals are not comparable across rows.

sources.name: Published training runs
sources.attribution: Model papers and cards, plus Epoch AI compute estimates.
sources.scope: 14 model training runs with parameters, tokens, FLOPs, hardware, chip-hours and MFU where published.
sources.caveats: Frontier labs stopped publishing compute after 2024, so later rows are reconstructions from hardware counts and durations.

sources.name: Compute map resolved sites
sources.scope: The identity layer: 631 canonical sites with their merge decisions, best coordinates and alias names, used as the prior for entity resolution rather than re-solving geographic dedup here.
sources.caveats: Derived, so it inherits every caveat of its four inputs. Used here for identity and geometry, not as an independent claim.

sources.name: Curated entity facts
sources.scope: Founding year, chief executive, headquarters and ticker for 35 companies, plus the category, role and constraint of 10 supply-chain components — attributes no ingested dataset in this repository carries.
sources.caveats: Hand-entered and undated: chief executives and tickers change. These are the only values in the registry with no document behind them.
